transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-30
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Amit Patel (Nimbus - Sr ML Eng), Sara Gomez (Nimbus - Platform Eng Manager), Ryan Chu (Nimbus - Security)

00:00 Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um I'm Jordan from Redwood, this is Priya our solutions engineer, we'll run through the console tracing + error analysis flows and then leave time for questions
00:12 Priya: hi all, hi, quick agenda, tracing overview, live walkthrough of traces and request logs, how to debug errors, and then we can dig into Dedicated vs hosted considerations
00:25 Amit: sounds good; our main ask is really latency and reproducibility for our fraud-detector flows, also we need to understand how trace context ties back to our logs
00:35 Jordan: great, thanks Amit; Sara, Ryan, feel free to jump in on security or infra questions at any point
00:39 Sara: yes, we'll ask about VPC, sso, and retention policy — and encryption, KMS, things like that
00:45 Priya: ok opening the Redwood Console now, bear with me -- first thing is the trace list, you'll see traces grouped by request-id, we show span timeline, token latency breakdown and model switch points
01:10 Priya: (screen) here is a sampled trace for a multi-turn chat request — you can see the per-token latency bars, we also show kernel-level notes when we detect quantized model variants, sometimes transcription shows model name as 'red wood-large' in older logs, apologies for the mismatch
01:35 Amit: how often do you sample? we need near-complete traces for the fraud pipeline otherwise we can't debug intermittent misses
01:42 Priya: good question — by default sampling is 10% for hosted, but for Dedicated you can bump to higher sampling or full tracing for specific routes; also we can enable request-level capture for a pilot
01:58 Jordan: and note we provide a per-route config to pin sampling up for a set of session ids or request tags, so you don't have to trace everything
02:12 Ryan: what about PII in request logs? we can't send raw payloads off-prem for some flows
02:18 Priya: right, so we have redact rules and field-level masking in request logs; for Private/Dedicated deployments you can keep logs inside customer VPC and integrate with your KMS/HSM — we store encryption metadata but customers manage keys if they want
02:36 Sara: is that supported with SSO? we use Okta and need SAML + SCIM for user provisioning
02:41 Jordan: yep, SSO via SAML and SCIM is supported, RBAC roles map to console features, and audit logs are available for admin actions
02:55 Amit: show me error analysis — we get weird hallucinated entity values that cause downstream rules to blow up, how do you surface that?
03:05 Priya: switching over — error analysis view groups by error signature, stack traces, model output diffs, and you can attach the exact request payload; we also highlight regression alerts if a prompt set drops below a quality threshold
03:28 Priya: (screen) here is an error grouping for 'entity-mismatch' — you can click one, see sample requests, response tokens, and an isolated diff between expected vs generated text; the UI tries to cluster by token-level differences but sometimes clusters are noisy, you'll see that in older projects
03:55 Amit: you said token-level differences; can we pivot to KV cache effects? sometimes the cache returns stale context
04:05 Priya: yes, KV cache is surfaced on spans that use cached KV entries — we annotate spans with cache-hit/cache-miss and give a timeline of when KV was populated. Note: sometimes transcription writes K V cache or K-V cash in older traces, the importer munged the field name once, we've fixed it but you might see odd labels in older logs
04:28 Sara: nice — can we export traces to our internal tracing system (we use Jaeger + Datadog)?
04:36 Priya: exports supported — you can forward spans to OTLP endpoints, and we have integrations for Datadog/Jaeger/Tempo; for Private deployments we can install a bridge inside your VPC
04:46 Amit: latency numbers — what's the per-token breakdown and how do we see kernel selection?
04:52 Priya: we show per-token latency bars and annotate when there's a model variant switch (e.g., redwood-vlq -> redwood-quant). Kernel selection notes appear as hint badges; and in Dedicated we can surface GPU kernel metrics if you enable agent telemetry
05:15 Jordan: typical tradeoff discussion — hosted is fastest to get started and costs are predictable per-token, Dedicated gives you reserved GPUs for predictable throughput and lower unit costs at scale, but you take on some ops config for autoscaling and policy tuning
05:34 Ryan: do you do mTLS between services? regs require mutual TLS to certain endpoints
05:40 Priya: yes, mutual TLS and private endpoints supported for Dedicated/Private; hosted APIs are over TLS; for extra security we can do customer-managed VPN peering and private link in some regions
05:58 Amit: what's the retention on request logs in hosted? we might need 13 months for compliance
06:04 Jordan: hosted default is 90 days, add-on for extended retention to 13 months or longer for enterprise customers — retention costs scale with storage but we can quote that; Private you can store indefinitely in your infra
06:18 Sara: ok show a debugging flow — we have a request that failed a rule downstream, we want to trace through from request to token generation to final response and the post-processing hook
06:27 Priya: sure — here's an example trace; first span is 'ingest', then 'model-invoke', then 'postprocess'; click into model-invoke and you can view request payload, prompt, model version, and the token stream; there's a 'request-id' that shows up in your app logs so you can correlate
06:49 Priya: notice the model-invoke span has multiple child spans for batching; when batching happens you'll see batch start/end markers — for debugging you can replay a single request through the 'replay' button which replays the prompt against the pinned model version
07:10 Amit: replay sounds useful — does it run against prod weights or a snapshot? we need deterministic reproductions
07:16 Priya: replay hits a snapshot of the model weights and execution environment taken at the time of the request; deterministic unless the model has non-deterministic layers, but we aim for parity
07:27 Ryan: what about pruning PII before storing logs? is there a transform pipeline?
07:33 Priya: yes, you can add pre-ingest transforms that redact or hash fields; we support regex-based and schema-based redaction, plus integration with enterprise DLP vendors if you need more advanced PII detection
07:47 Sara: can we restrict who can view raw payloads in the Console? we need least-privilege
07:51 Jordan: yes, RBAC controls viewing of request logs and traces, with audit trails for who accessed what and when
08:05 Amit: how do you surface model quality regressions? we have periodic evals and want alerts if the model drifts
08:12 Priya: Redwood Optimize ties into the Console — you can create prompt evals, run against golden datasets, and get regression alerts; in the error analysis view you can pin a prompt set and get time series charts for pass/fail rate
08:30 Amit: any way to attach our own scorer? we have custom business logic for scoring responses
08:35 Priya: you can upload a custom scorer as a lambda-style function or point to a webhook; then the eval pipeline will call your scorer and surface metrics
08:44 Sara: ok show me a real request log entry
08:46 Priya: (screen) here's the request log, timestamp, route, incoming headers, user metadata, and the input prompt. Note: headers sometimes get normalized differently depending on proxy, so you may see x-request-id vs request-id variants in older logs
09:10 Priya: you can also filter by response status (200, 500), by model version, by route, or by custom tags — and combine filters to narrow to exactly the failed requests
09:22 Amit: how quickly can you turn on full capture for a route? we might want to capture all requests for a short experiment
09:27 Jordan: for Dedicated we can flip it on in config immediately; hosted requires a policy change but we can enable request-level capture for a customer during a pilot window
09:36 Ryan: does full capture increase latency? we're worried about tail latencies
09:40 Priya: capture itself is asynchronous for payload storage; tracing adds some overhead to spans but we try to keep overhead minimal — for high-SLA routes we recommend sampling high but not 100% capture of full payloads, or using selective capture for error cases only
09:56 Amit: ok can you show an example where batching caused increased latency? we had a batch scenario where 1 slow request slowed the whole batch and it was hard to isolate
10:05 Priya: here, this trace shows batch start at 00:00:12, one child span had a long pre-processing and pushed tail latency up; Console flags slowoutlier children and you can drill into token timing and pre/post hooks to see where time was spent
10:26 Sara: curious about model switching fallbacks — you said Redwood can fallback to cheaper variants when capacity constrained? how is that visible in traces?
10:33 Priya: yes, smart routing can fall back; traces annotate fallback reason and model variant chosen; and you can set per-route policy to allow or disallow fallbacks; in error analysis we surface quality regression alerts when a fallback changes output characteristics significantly
10:50 Amit: any misconception folks usually have about the Console?
10:53 Priya: usually people expect traces to be perfect — there are occasional importer naming mismatches (model names, k v cache labels) and sampling artifacts; we try to be explicit about sampling and retention limits
11:05 Jordan: quick pause for questions
11:10 Ryan: SOC2 — can Redwood provide reports and do you support customer-managed keys?
11:15 Jordan: yes SOC2 Type II available; for encryption we support customer-managed KMS in Dedicated/Private and envelope encryption for hosted; we'll send whitepaper and the security pack after this call
11:26 Sara: where do audit logs live? separate from request logs?
11:30 Priya: audit logs for console actions are stored separately and can be forwarded to your SIEM; request logs are request-level and have separate retention and access controls
11:42 Amit: pricing — can you ballpark Dedicated committed pricing vs hosted per-token for our estimated 10M tokens/month?
11:51 Jordan: rough numbers in chat: hosted per-token at list is higher but no infra commitment; Dedicated reserved capacity at that volume typically lowers unit cost 25-40% depending on GPU mixes and utilization — we'll follow up with exact quote tailored to your workload
12:12 Priya: back to demo, here's a request log with the replay button clicked, it shows the exact prompt context and the option to replay against same model snapshot or a canary bucket
12:35 Amit: can traces link to our internal incident tracker? we want automatic ticket create when an error signature spikes
12:41 Priya: yes, alerting hooks can call webhooks to create tickets in Jira or ServiceNow, and you can configure thresholds on grouped error signatures
12:52 Sara: for the pilot, we want sample dashboards showing latency percentiles, error rates, and a trace sampler view — can you provision that?
12:58 Jordan: yes we can pre-configure dashboards for the pilot and share a read-only link; Priya will include sample dashboards in the runbook
13:08 Amit: a few minor nitpicks — sometimes the token timelines compress on narrow screens and it's hard to see per-token spikes, also I saw an odd label 'red wool' in earlier trace exports, likely transcription
13:22 Priya: noted, UI improvements are ongoing, and we can surface raw token timestamps in the export for offline analysis
13:33 Jordan: ok let's do a recap: Redwood to share SOC2 + security docs, Priya to share benchmark runbook and dashboards, Nimbus to provide test prompt set and SLAs, we'll schedule pilot for week of 2026-06-08 and follow up on 2026-06-11. Any other questions?
13:56 Ryan: nothing else from security, thanks
14:00 Sara: thank you, useful overview
14:05 Amit: thanks everyone, look forward to the runbook
14:10 Jordan: great, thanks all, we'll send the notes and next steps
14:15 End of recording
